title: What is known about 1RB0LF_0RC0LC_1LA1LD_1RE1LC_---1RA_0LC0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_0RC0LC_1LA1LD_1RE1LC_---1RA_0LC0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Almost the whole tape is the seven-cell word 0101111 (five 1s) in one of its seven phases. Long runs of it are separated by a handful of short defects. Two crossings of a run are proved in Lean. The defects' dynamics, and with it halting (E reading a 0), is not understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,333 cells have been visited and 47,383 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.148). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine halts only when E reads a 0. E is entered from D on a 0 (writing 1, moving right), and the sweeps run the zigzag D, C, A, E through the defects. A halt would need a defect shape not seen so far. Ruling it out needs the defect dynamics. CTL (windows of 2 to 5 cells) and NGramCPS (widths 2 to 8, history, LRU) fail.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1RD_1LC0RF_0LA0RA_1LE1RA_---1LB_0RA0LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: B and C crossing whole runs of the period-7 word.
No halt in the C simulator; 66,333 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A period-7 word in many phases
html: Every run is the same word 0101111 read from a different starting cell. Between the runs sit defects of a few cells: 1^5, 10 1^5, 01011 01011, 1^7. A sweep shifts each run by one or two cells as it passes. B and C cross a whole run in one go (proved in Lean); on the way back, a zigzag of D, C, A, E converts runs two copies at a time.

sections.heading: What changes
html:
Each sweep moves the defects a little and the runs grow at the expense of their neighbours. New runs appear at the right end, where the bouncer adds cells, and the right side grows like the square root of the step count. The run lengths (302, 191, 1,341, 1,001, 731, 753, 3,767, 1,382 above) do not follow any visible rule.

What halting would need. E reading a 0. This would be a defect arrangement that sends D onto a 0 next to a 0. The pattern resembles 1RB1LE_1RC1RF_0RD0LB_1LD0RA_0LA0LE_0RC--- of the same batch (period 24). A shared method would be a CTL whose automaton reads the tape in words of the period and admits a finite list of defects.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.148). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.553).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,333 cells (447 left of the start, 49,079 right), with a density of 1s of 0.714.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: The tape is the seven-cell word 0101111 repeated, cut into long runs in different phases by short defects; the sweeps carry runs across in one go and slowly move and lengthen them, and the run lengths look irregular.
